report:
Your skepticism is well-founded — this claim is false, and it's been thoroughly debunked by health authorities and fact-checkers since early 2020.

**What the evidence shows:**

The World Health Organization directly addressed this claim in its COVID-19 "Mythbusters" series, stating that while garlic "is a healthy food that may have some antimicrobial properties," there is "no evidence from the current outbreak that eating garlic has protected people from the new coronavirus" (https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters).

FactCheck.org specifically investigated the "boiled garlic water" claim as it spread on social media in February 2020, concluding: "Online posts falsely claim the new coronavirus can be cured by drinking one bowl of freshly boiled garlic water. That's not true; there is no cure for the virus" (https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/).

AFP Fact Check similarly reported that health professionals confirmed as early as February 2020 there was "no evidence for its use as an effective treatment," and this finding held even years later when a garlic-industry-funded lab study was misrepresented as showing garlic outperformed vaccines — the very institute that ran the study clarified its results did not support any medical treatment application (https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19).

**Why the claim persists:** Garlic does contain allicin, a compound with documented antimicrobial properties in laboratory (in vitro) settings. This kernel of real chemistry gets exaggerated into false clinical claims, but no human trials have demonstrated that drinking garlic water treats or cures COVID-19.

**Conclusion:** The claim is false and has been consistently rated as misinformation by WHO, FactCheck.org, AFP, and other fact-checking organizations. No boiled garlic preparation cures, treats, or prevents COVID-19; relying on it instead of proven medical care could be harmful.
